timeline.current_model: PARK7/DJ-1 is a multifunctional homodimeric protein whose activity is regulated by oxidation of the conserved Cys106 residue; it functions as an oxidative stress sensor and antioxidant that: (1) binds and inhibits the 20S proteasome to protect partially unfolded proteins from degradation; (2) promotes Nrf2 nuclear translocation and ARE-dependent transcription (including thioredoxin 1) to upregulate antioxidant defenses; (3) binds subunits of mitochondrial Complex I (NDUFA4, ND1) to maintain its activity; (4) acts downstream of PINK1/parkin to facilitate optineurin recruitment and selective mitophagy; (5) binds PDHB to inhibit PDHA phosphorylation and promote pyruvate dehydrogenase activity and OXPHOS in Treg cells; (6) stabilizes HIF-1α by interacting with VHL and inhibiting its E3 ligase activity; (7) preserves the SAHH tetramer to support transsulfuration/glutathione biosynthesis and suppress ferroptosis; (8) binds BCL-XL in an oxidation-dependent manner to stabilize it and suppress apoptosis; (9) inhibits RANKL-driven osteoclastogenesis via SHP-1 activation; (10) acts as an extracellular DAMP activating TLR2/TLR4 when released from necrotic cells; and (11) is secreted via an autophagy-based unconventional pathway in response to oxidative stress.
